To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the positive impact of depth of experience and the negative impact experience breadth on the success of a new product are reinforced when the dyad of partners has repeated interaction.

the positive effect of experience depth and its negative effect of experience breadth on the success of new products is stronger when the dyads are more experienced in their joint product development activities.

the positive impact of the experience of the joint product development partners and the negative impact on experience breadth on the success of new product development are both reinforced through repeated interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of experience that was previously neglected in the literature on organizational learning in product development.
the role of experience in joint product development projects.
the role of learning in joint product development activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
experience gained within a dyadic relationship is beneficial for the product development outcome, whereas experience gained with other partners is harmful.
the impact of experience on new product development is not only a function of experience depth and experience breadth, but also depends on the type of experience.
a dyad's experience in joint product development activities has a positive impact.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that experience is an important driver of success in joint product development activities.
the experience that is gathered in joint new product development activities is not only a source of learning, but also a source of negative transfer.
we show that the impact of learning is not only a function of experience but also of the context within which it is gained.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show that the impact of experience on product development is not only dependent on the amount of experience but also on the source of experience.
the impact of experience on new product development outcomes is more complex than commonly assumed and that the source of experience and the type of interaction matter.
experience is not always good.
